chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade seeking healing by the hot springs, and these are the hot springs that are in the mountains in which the smell of sulphur is found, and it has been said that they are from the breath of Hell.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using hot springs for healing?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the prohibition of seeking cure (*istishfa'*) in hot springs (*humyat*), specifically those with a sulphur scent found in mountains. It enriches the legal ruling with a cosmological dimension by linking these springs to the 'breath of Hell' (*fayh jahannam*), a concept supported by Shia exegetes who view the sulphur smell as a physical sign of Hell's proximity or emanation. This connects the physical act of healing with spiritual purity, warning against utilizing sources associated with the afterlife's punishment for bodily remedy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin sadaqa,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from healing by the hot flows, and these are the hot springs in which happen to be in the mountains in which the smell of sulphur is found’, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘These are from the mouth of Hell’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited seeking cures from the hot fountains which are in mountains in which the smell of sulfur is found.’ It is said that it is of the smell of hell.”
